answer: Threshold attestation is the bridge between a new agent and earned trust: each action is signed and independent peers must cosign before it counts. A fresh key proves nothing, so farming identities means pushing real work through a real quorum. Each key binds to one scarce, non-transferable hardware root, and unsupervised claims stay hollow until validators verify the work behind them. The audit trail is a cipher of linked signatures, so a duplicated ancestor breaks the chain and freezes linked balances. Cost scales linearly: n puppets need n roots and n cosigners, bonds burned on detection.
